investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with an Unschedulable verdict: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because agent creation never progressed past the scheduling gate.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 eligible peer-pod nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable capacity exists for new peer-pod VMs and that preemption cannot recover capacity. Because the pod never became Running, the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never returned an agent, so all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) remained absent and the expected-output contract (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json lines 254–259) was fully violated. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: [Highest confidence] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on the 2 eligible peer-pod nodes — all concurrent or lingering remote-agent pods have claimed all available VM slots, leaving zero capacity for new probe pods. Preemption was explicitly ruled out by the scheduler.
[Medium confidence] A prior eval run or a production workload left orphaned peer-pod VMs running, consuming the extended resource without releasing it, preventing the probe from acquiring a slot.

[Medium confidence] The 4 non-peer-pod nodes have a node affinity or node selector mismatch (e.g., a label like kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable=true is absent) that permanently excludes them from scheduling remote-agent pods, reducing effective capacity to only 2 nodes.
[Lower confidence] The cluster was scaled down or a peer-pod node was cordoned/drained, reducing the total kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity below the demand level at the time of the eval run.

investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-08-15 with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not place the eval pod because 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) never completed, leaving all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) unpopulated and causing the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 264 to fail entirely.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent eval environment has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that carry that resource class. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every attempt to provision a remote agent VM during the eval window results in an Unschedulable pod that times out (~138–143 s), preventing the runner from collecting any evidence. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents eval path in production-api; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

All three sibling checks share this exact message, confirming the resource pool was fully consumed for the entire eval window.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes never matched the pod's affinity rules, meaning only 2 nodes are ever eligible. If those 2 nodes lose capacity simultaneously (e.g., a prior eval's cleanup did not release the vm resource), the cluster has no fallback. A change to node labels or pod affinity rules could have reduced the eligible node count.

TERTIARY — VM resource leak from a prior eval run that did not complete cleanup: the withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs is responsible for releasing resources; if a previous run was interrupted before cleanup, vm slots may remain allocated, starving subsequent runs.
LOWER — Cluster node count reduction: if the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes were recently cordoned, drained, or removed, available capacity would drop to zero without any code change.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with an Unschedulable verdict: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because agent creation never progressed past the scheduling gate.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 eligible peer-pod nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable capacity exists for new peer-pod VMs and that preemption cannot recover capacity. Because the pod never became Running, the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never returned an agent, so all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) remained absent and the expected-output contract (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json lines 254–259) was fully violated. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-08-15 with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not place the eval pod because 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) never completed, leaving all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) unpopulated and causing the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 264 to fail entirely.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent eval environment has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that carry that resource class. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every attempt to provision a remote agent VM during the eval window results in an Unschedulable pod that times out (~138–143 s), preventing the runner from collecting any evidence. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents eval path in production-api; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

All three sibling checks share this exact message, confirming the resource pool was fully consumed for the entire eval window.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes never matched the pod's affinity rules, meaning only 2 nodes are ever eligible. If those 2 nodes lose capacity simultaneously (e.g., a prior eval's cleanup did not release the vm resource), the cluster has no fallback. A change to node labels or pod affinity rules could have reduced the eligible node count.

TERTIARY — VM resource leak from a prior eval run that did not complete cleanup: the withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs is responsible for releasing resources; if a previous run was interrupted before cleanup, vm slots may remain allocated, starving subsequent runs.
LOWER — Cluster node count reduction: if the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes were recently cordoned, drained, or removed, available capacity would drop to zero without any code change.

All other public-website sibling checks passed, isolating the failure to the snapshot publication pipeline rather than the public web surface itself.

The snapshot file is reachable and structurally valid (all required evidence fields are present, source=github-actions, hasLiveSource=true, generatedAtPresent=true), but its embedded generation timestamp is stale by more than double the allowed 300-minute window. This is an eval-layer signal of a workflow scheduling or execution gap; no evidence of a user-facing outage on the public website pages is present.
